---- MODULE W4Od12m4p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

Requests == {"r1", "r2", "r3"}
MaxCap == 3
MinCap == 1

VARIABLES queue, served, cap, admitted, worked

vars == <<queue, served, cap, admitted, worked>>

InQueue(r) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] = r

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Requests)
    /\ served \subseteq Requests
    /\ admitted \subseteq Requests
    /\ cap \in MinCap..MaxCap
    /\ worked \in 0..9

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ served = {}
    /\ admitted = {}
    /\ cap = MinCap
    /\ worked = 0

AdmitRequest(r) ==
    /\ r \notin admitted
    /\ Len(queue) < cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
    /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, cap, worked>>

Transfuse ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET r == Head(queue) IN
        /\ served' = served \cup {r}
        /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ worked' = worked + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, admitted>>

RaiseCapacity ==
    /\ cap < MaxCap
    /\ cap' = cap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, served, admitted, worked>>

LowerCapacity ==
    /\ cap > MinCap
    /\ cap' = cap - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, served, admitted, worked>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Requests : AdmitRequest(r)
    \/ Transfuse
    \/ RaiseCapacity
    \/ LowerCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ServedNotPending == \A r \in served : ~InQueue(r)

====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker admits transfusion requests into a bounded work queue.
Each request names a blood unit. The queue has a runtime-adjustable capacity: an operator
may raise or lower the admission ceiling while the system runs. Admission applies
backpressure -- a new request is refused (dropped, not queued) whenever the number of
queued requests already meets the current capacity. A worker pulls the head request off
the queue and performs the transfusion, which is irreversible: the request's unit is
consumed and the request is marked served exactly once, then it leaves the queue. The
operator may also lower capacity below the current queue depth; queued requests already
admitted are honored, no admitted request is silently discarded.

Actions: AdmitRequest (enqueue under backpressure), Transfuse (irreversible serve of head),
RaiseCapacity, LowerCapacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A request that has been served (its irreversible transfusion done) never
still appears as pending in the work queue.

---- MODULE W4Od5m8p0t0 ----
EXTENDS FiniteSets

Players == {"p1", "p2", "p3"}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, owner, pstate, crashed

vars == <<coarse, owner, pstate, crashed>>

States == {"idle", "hasCoarse", "critical"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Players \cup {NONE}
    /\ owner \in Players \cup {NONE}
    /\ pstate \in [Players -> States]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Players

Init ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ pstate = [p \in Players |-> "idle"]
    /\ crashed = {}

AcquireCoarse(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ pstate[p] = "idle"
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ coarse' = p
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "hasCoarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, crashed>>

AcquireFine(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ pstate[p] = "hasCoarse"
    /\ coarse = p
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ owner' = p
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "critical"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, crashed>>

ReleaseAll(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ pstate[p] = "critical"
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ coarse' = NONE
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed>>

Crash(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ pstate[p] # "idle"
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, owner, pstate>>

Reclaim(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ \E c \in crashed :
        /\ coarse = c
        /\ coarse' = NONE
        /\ owner' = IF owner = c THEN NONE ELSE owner
        /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
        /\ crashed' = crashed \ {c}

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players : AcquireCoarse(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : AcquireFine(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : ReleaseAll(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Crash(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Reclaim(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualExclusion == \A p \in Players : pstate[p] = "critical" => owner = p

====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker guards a single shared match-server slot using a
two-level hierarchical lock: a player must first take the coarse region lock, then the
fine slot lock, before entering the critical section that binds the match server. A
player can crash silently at any point while holding locks -- it simply stops, still
appearing to hold whatever it held. To avoid the lobby wedging forever, a healthy player
may reclaim the region from a crashed holder, which fully releases that crashed player's
coarse and (if held) fine locks and clears its crash flag.

Actions: AcquireCoarse, AcquireFine (enter critical section), ReleaseAll, Crash (silent),
Reclaim (recovery of a crashed holder's locks).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a player is in the critical section, it is the sole owner of the
shared match-server slot -- no two players ever hold the slot at once.

====
nl:
A subway signalling block system hands out track-occupancy permits from one shared pool.
Two independent signalling instances, A and B, both draw from and return to the same pool
by compare-and-swap on a shared register that holds the current free-permit count: an
acquire reads the count and swaps it to count-1 only if unchanged, a release swaps it up
by one. Each successful swap bumps a version stamp. Permits are neither created nor lost --
every permit is either free in the pool or held by exactly one instance.

Actions: AcquireA, ReleaseA, AcquireB, ReleaseB.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free permits plus those held by instance A plus those held
by instance B always equals the fixed total number of permits.

Nodes == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
NONE == "none"
MAXTERM == 3

VARIABLES term, activeLeader, role, myTerm, unlockHolder

vars == <<term, activeLeader, role, myTerm, unlockHolder>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MAXTERM
    /\ activeLeader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ role \in [Nodes -> {"follower", "leader"}]
    /\ myTerm \in [Nodes -> 0..MAXTERM]
    /\ unlockHolder \in Nodes \cup {NONE}

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ activeLeader = NONE
    /\ role = [n \in Nodes |-> "follower"]
    /\ myTerm = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ unlockHolder = NONE

Elect(n) ==
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MAXTERM + 1)
    /\ activeLeader' = n
    /\ role' = [m \in Nodes |-> IF m = n THEN "leader" ELSE "follower"]
    /\ myTerm' = [myTerm EXCEPT ![n] = (term + 1) % (MAXTERM + 1)]
    /\ unlockHolder' = NONE

StepDown(n) ==
    /\ role[n] = "leader"
    /\ activeLeader = n
    /\ role' = [role EXCEPT ![n] = "follower"]
    /\ activeLeader' = NONE
    /\ unlockHolder' = IF unlockHolder = n THEN NONE ELSE unlockHolder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, myTerm>>

SyncTerm(n) ==
    /\ myTerm[n] < term
    /\ myTerm' = [myTerm EXCEPT ![n] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, activeLeader, role, unlockHolder>>

Unlock(n) ==
    /\ activeLeader = n
    /\ role[n] = "leader"
    /\ myTerm[n] = term
    /\ unlockHolder = NONE
    /\ unlockHolder' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, activeLeader, role, myTerm>>

Relock(n) ==
    /\ unlockHolder = n
    /\ unlockHolder' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, activeLeader, role, myTerm>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : StepDown(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : SyncTerm(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Unlock(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Relock(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SingleUnlocker ==
    unlockHolder # NONE => (unlockHolder = activeLeader /\ role[unlockHolder] = "leader")

====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network elects one leader controller that alone holds the right to
disengage the deadbolt. Elections are epoch-numbered; on failover a new controller wins a
fresh epoch and becomes the active leader, demoting the others to followers. A controller
can be slow but never truly fails: a lagging follower may carry a stale epoch number, and
it can later sync its epoch up to the current one. Only the current active leader, on the
current epoch, may seize the unlock right; a slow node carrying an old epoch cannot.

Actions: Elect (failover to a new epoch leader), StepDown, SyncTerm (slow follower catches
its epoch up), Unlock (seize unlock right), Relock (release unlock right).

SAFETY PROPERTY: If the unlock right is held, it is held by the current active leader and
no one else.

====
nl:
A print-shop job spooler runs two independent spooler instances, A and B, that draw
printer slots from one shared pool. To avoid conflicts, the instances elect a single
leader; only the current leader may allocate a slot to a job. Elections are epoch-numbered
and support failover -- the leader may step down and a new leader is elected. When the
leader allocates a free slot to a waiting job, that job records the slot and the slot
records its job. A job releases its slot when its print finishes.

Actions: Elect (epoch-numbered, either instance), StepDown (failover), Allocate (leader
gives a free slot to a job), Release (job frees its slot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job that holds a slot is recorded as that slot's sole owner, so no
slot is ever allocated to two jobs at once.

Requests == {"r1", "r2", "r3", "r4"}
CAP == 2

VARIABLES pending, inflight, done, rejected

vars == <<pending, inflight, done, rejected>>

Occupancy == Cardinality(pending) + Cardinality(inflight)

TypeOK ==
    /\ pending \subseteq Requests
    /\ inflight \subseteq Requests
    /\ done \subseteq Requests
    /\ rejected \subseteq Requests

Init ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ done = {}
    /\ rejected = {}

Fresh(r) == r \notin pending /\ r \notin inflight /\ r \notin done /\ r \notin rejected

Admit(r) ==
    /\ Fresh(r)
    /\ Occupancy < CAP
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, done, rejected>>

Reject(r) ==
    /\ Fresh(r)
    /\ Occupancy >= CAP
    /\ rejected' = rejected \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, inflight, done>>

Dispatch(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, rejected>>

Complete(r) ==
    /\ r \in inflight
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {r}
    /\ done' = done \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, rejected>>

Reset(r) ==
    /\ r \in (done \cup rejected)
    /\ done' = done \ {r}
    /\ rejected' = rejected \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, inflight>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Admit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Reset(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Reject(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Dispatch(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Complete(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityBound == Occupancy <= CAP

====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser feeds fill requests through a bounded work queue with
backpressure. The combined number of requests waiting plus those actively being filled may
never exceed a fixed capacity. Because requests arrive over an unreliable channel, they may
be reordered: a pharmacist may pick ANY waiting request to start filling, not necessarily
the oldest. When the queue-plus-inflight is at capacity, a new request is refused by
backpressure and recorded as rejected rather than admitted.

Actions: Admit (accept a request when below capacity), Reject (backpressure refusal when at
capacity), Dispatch (begin filling any waiting request, out of order), Complete (finish a
fill), Reset (a completed or rejected prescription is returned to the fresh pool for a
later refill).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of waiting requests plus the number of in-flight fills never
exceeds the fixed capacity.

    /\ filled' = filled + 1

====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction matches a fixed number of share lots. A single auction
coordinator is elected (epoch-numbered, with failover) and alone may match lots. Each lot
lives in exactly one of three states: unfilled, matching (tentatively paired, awaiting
member confirmation), or filled. The coordinator moves an unfilled lot into matching. A
member can be slow but never fails: it may confirm a matching lot late, moving it to
filled. If the coordinator fails over before a confirmation lands, a matching lot is
unwound back to unfilled. No lot is ever created or destroyed.

Actions: Elect (epoch-numbered coordinator election / failover), StepDown, Match
(coordinator tentatively pairs an unfilled lot), Confirm (a slow member finalizes a match),
Unwind (a matching lot returns to unfilled).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of unfilled, matching, and filled lots always sums to the fixed
total number of lots.

====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch moves funds through a pipeline shared by two
independent bank instances, A and B, that draw on one common pool of settlement units.
Units start held at bank A, are sent into an in-flight state, are received at bank B, may
be sent back into flight from B, and are finally settled (removed from active circulation
but still accounted for). Settlement runs under epoch-numbered reconfiguration: finalizing
a unit is only permitted while the settlement window is open, which toggles with the epoch.
Units are conserved end to end -- none are created or lost.

Actions: Reconfigure (advance the epoch, toggling the settlement window), SendFromA,
ReceiveAtB, SendFromB, Finalize (settle a unit while the window is open).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units held at A, held at B, in flight, and settled always sum to the
fixed batch total.

====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet has two independent controllers, A and B, that pick and stow items
from one shared shelf pool using optimistic locking with retry. Each controller first reads
the shelf's version stamp; it may then commit a pick or a stow only if the stamp is still
the one it read. A successful pick or stow bumps the version stamp, so a controller whose
read is now stale must re-read (retry) before it can act again. Items are conserved: every
item is either on the shelf or carried by exactly one controller.

Actions: ReadA, ReadB (snapshot the version), PickA, PickB (optimistic pick if version
unchanged), DropA, DropB (optimistic stow if version unchanged).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The items on the shelf plus those carried by A plus those carried by B
always equal the fixed total number of items.

====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser is organized as a token ring of dispensing stations. A
single token circulates the ring; only the station currently holding the token may dispense
a pill from the shared stock, granting exclusive access. Dispensed pills move from stock to
a dispensed tally, and returned pills move back. A runtime-adjustable capacity caps how many
pills may be outstanding as dispensed at once; an operator may raise or lower this capacity
while the ring runs. Pills are conserved -- each pill is either in stock or dispensed.

Actions: PassToken (advance the token to the next station on the ring), Dispense (token
holder moves a pill from stock to dispensed, staying within capacity), Return (a dispensed
pill goes back to stock), ChangeCapacity (operator resets the outstanding-dispensed cap).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The pills in stock plus the pills dispensed always equal the fixed total
number of pills.

    IF m.op # NONEOP /\ m.rv = ver /\ m.op = "issue" /\ fr > 0

    ELSE IF m.op # NONEOP /\ m.rv = ver /\ m.op = "restock" /\ is > 0

    /\ UNCHANGED slotB

(apply or discard the slot's message, in any order).

number of units.

    /\ crashed = {}

    /\ leaseHolder = NONE
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ leaseHolder' = c
    /\ ttl' = L
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acting, crashed>>

    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ ttl' = ttl - 1
    /\ leaseHolder' = IF ttl - 1 = 0 THEN NONE ELSE leaseHolder
    /\ acting' = IF ttl - 1 = 0 THEN NONE ELSE acting
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Act(c) ==
    /\ leaseHolder = c
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ acting' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, ttl, crashed>>

Release(c) ==
    /\ leaseHolder = c
    /\ leaseHolder' = NONE
    /\ ttl' = 0
    /\ acting' = IF acting = c THEN NONE ELSE acting
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Crash(c) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, ttl, acting>>

Recover(c) ==
    /\ c \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, ttl, acting>>

    \/ Tick
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Act(c)

    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Recover(c)

====
nl:
A power-grid load shedder authorizes load-shedding only to the controller currently holding
a valid lease. A lease is granted with a fixed time-to-live and expires as time ticks; when
it expires, the actuator is disengaged. Only the lease holder, while its lease is still
valid, may engage the shed actuator -- a controller with an expired (stale) lease, or one
that never held the lease, must not act. One controller may crash silently while holding the
lease; it stops working but its lease is not released early, only expiring on its own, and a
crashed controller may later recover.

Actions: Grant (give the free lease to a controller), Tick (advance time, expiring the lease
and disengaging the actuator when its time runs out), Act (the valid lease holder engages
the shed actuator), Release (the holder gives up its lease and disengages), Crash (one
controller fails silently), Recover (a crashed controller returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the shed actuator is engaged, it is engaged by the current lease
holder whose lease is still valid -- never by a stale or unauthorized controller.

A pharmacy prescription dispenser fills controlled-substance prescriptions. Dispensing a
prescription is irreversible and must happen at most once. Filling uses optimistic locking:
when a prescription is requested it snapshots a version stamp; a pharmacist may dispense it
only if the stamp is still current, and each dispense bumps the stamp so any concurrent

disable override), AdminOverride (force a dispense of a waiting prescription, bypassing the
version check).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No prescription is ever both waiting and already dispensed -- each
irreversible dispense happens at most once.

nl:
A vending machine network updates one shared inventory record through a bounded work queue
with backpressure. Each update job, when enqueued, snapshots the current record and its
version stamp; the queue has a fixed capacity, and a job is refused (not enqueued) when the
queue is full. A worker applies the head job only if its snapshotted version still matches
the live version -- then it writes back its snapshot plus its entry and bumps the version;
if the snapshot is stale the head job is discarded and must be re-enqueued (retry). A
privileged operator may enable an admin override and write a fresh entry directly, bypassing
the queue, but such a write is always based on the current record so it never loses an
update.

head job if its version is current), Discard (drop a stale head job), ToggleAdmin (enable or
disable override), AdminOverride (operator writes a fresh entry directly, bypassing the
queue).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry that has been committed is still present in the shared inventory
record -- no committed update is ever lost.

returns).

book -- no accepted order is ever lost by a stale overwrite.
